name: Pernambuco
summary_text: Pernambuco recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, placing it in the second tier behind Ceará/Minas Gerais. Against a population of ~9.4 million this yields roughly 0.74 per million per year—nearly double the national rate. Crucially, the state hosts the major tourist corridor of Recife and Olinda, so the violence concentration directly overlaps with visitor traffic and visible trans presence in public coastal spaces. The rate and tourism overlap put Pernambuco about 0.07 below the national 0.71. Compared with Bahia (0.65), which also recorded 7 killings in 2025, Bahia's larger population (~15 M) gives a lower per-capita rate of ~0.47/million; Pernambuco's risk density is therefore somewhat higher despite the identical absolute count, and both states share the visitor-coast exposure. No Pernambuco-specific legal restriction or ordinance was found. The deviation is violence-driven and location-dependent: a trans visitor staying in Recife's centre or the Olinda historic district is in the same geography where the killings cluster.

sources.title: Brasil lidera ranking mundial de assassinatos de pessoas trans | SBT News
sources.claim_summary: SBT News report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th edition of the ANTRA dossier: Brazil recorded 80 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, down 34% on 2024, still the world's highest; state counts for 2025 - Ceará and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7, Goiás/Maranhão/Pará 5, Paraíba, Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte and São Paulo 4 each, Mato Grosso and Rio de Janeiro 3, Alagoas, Distrito Federal, Espírito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul 2; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (~140/yr); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, 70% Black, 67.5% committed outside state capitals.
